target.title: fix(web-search): align credential presence with usable providers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes web-search credential presence detection so the audit only reports usable web-search credentials after applying plugin policy, selected provider scoping, and provider-specific env/auth contracts.

The earlier detector could treat credentials from blocked plugins or unrelated providers as web-search credentials. The latest fix also handles the Google plugin's split contracts: selecting `gemini` no longer counts `google-vertex` env such as `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` as a Gemini web-search key.

## Why This Change Was Made

Security/audit surfaces should reflect the selected web-search provider's actual runtime credential contract. Plugin manifests can contain multiple providers and env vars, so manifest env scanning must not flatten unrelated provider credentials into one web-search-positive result.

## User Impact

- Disabled, denied, or non-selected web-search plugins no longer make `web_search` look credentialed.
- Missing env-backed SecretRefs fail closed consistently.
- `tools.web.search.provider: "gemini"` with only `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` no longer reports Gemini web search as configured.
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` still reports Gemini web search as configured through the selected provider contract.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 26 tests.

## Proof

- Provider-scoped manifest env detection now first reads the selected bundled web-search provider's public contract env vars, then falls back only to same-provider manifest setup/auth env metadata when a public contract is unavailable.
- Existing policy/credential tests still cover plugin allow/deny, disabled entries, keyless providers, raw plugin webSearch credentials, SecretRefs, and explicit provider selection.

target.title: fix: protect SMS webhook callback quota [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where invalid SMS webhook posts could consume the same inbound callback quota used by signed Twilio callbacks when deployments receive traffic through a shared proxy address.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SMS webhook now parses and validates Twilio-signed form requests, confirms the configured account, and only then applies the fixed-window quota. The quota key is scoped to the SMS account and webhook route plus the client address so one account path cannot consume another account path's quota.

## User Impact

Operators using the SMS plugin keep the same Twilio signature validation and webhook responses, while invalid unsigned traffic no longer burns the quota for later valid callbacks. High-volume valid signed callbacks are still rate-limited per account route.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(browser): invalidate stale roleRefs on main-frame navigation
target.body:
Closes: N/A (source-first bug fix)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where browser role refs (`e1`, `e2`, …) from a snapshot taken on page A could resolve to wrong elements on page B after a main-frame navigation. Three cached fields were stale after navigation: `state.roleRefs`, `state.roleRefsMode`/`state.roleRefsFrameSelector`, and the cross-Page `roleRefsByTarget` cache.

Additionally, the v1 fix stored navigation generation per-`PageState`, but `roleRefsByTarget` is intentionally shared across replacement `Page` objects. A replacement Page starting at generation zero could restore stale pre-navigation refs or reject fresh post-navigation refs.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. **framenavigated listener** clears `roleRefs`/`roleRefsMode`/`roleRefsFrameSelector` on main-frame navigation
2. **Target-scoped navGen** (`navGenerationByTarget` map keyed by `cdpUrl+targetId`) shared across replacement Pages via `pageTargetKeys` WeakMap
3. **Eviction** of `navGenerationByTarget` entries alongside `roleRefsByTarget` eviction (prevents unbounded map growth)
4. **restore guard** compares cached navGen with current target generation

## User Impact

- Stale refs after navigation throw "Unknown ref" instead of silently clicking wrong elements
- Replacement Page objects correctly share navigation lifecycle
- No impact on subframe navigations, page close, or existing workflows

## Real behavior proof

### Real Chrome/CDP proof (Google Chrome 138 + Playwright CDP)
```
Real Chrome/CDP proof: roleRefs invalidation on navigation

[phase 1] Snapshot on Page A
  Page A loaded: file:///tmp/.../page-a.html
  ok: refLocator resolves e1 on page A

[phase 2] Navigate to Page B
  Page B loaded: file:///tmp/.../page-b.html
  ok: FIXED: refLocator throws Unknown ref after navigation (stale ref rejected)
  ok: FIXED: refLocator throws Unknown ref for e2 too

[phase 3] Fresh snapshot on Page B
  ok: fresh snapshot stores refs on Page B

[phase 4] Replacement Page (new Page for same target)
  ok: replacement Page restores refs for same target

[phase 5] Navigate back to Page A
  ok: FIXED: refs cleared after second navigation
  ok: re-snapshot after second navigation works

Environment: Google Chrome 138 + Playwright CDP
ALL REAL CHROME PROOF ASSERTIONS: 7 passed, 0 failed
```

### Synthetic proof (real production functions + fake Page events): 21/21
Proof covers role-mode clear, aria-mode clear, frameSelector clear, subframe preserve, close cleanup, re-snapshot, navGen guard, replacement-Page stale reject, replacement-Page fresh restore.

### Negative control (per-PageState navGen reverted): 20/21
Confirmed v1 defect: replacement Page restores stale gen-0 cache after target navigation.

### Vitest: 91 passed (5 files)
37 tests in pw-session.test.ts (4 replacement-Page scenarios, navGen eviction coverage)

## Evidence

- **Real Chrome/CDP:** 7 assertions across 5 phases — navigation, stale rejection, fresh snapshot, replacement Page, second navigation
- **Synthetic:** 21/21 positive, 20/21 negative control (v1 defect confirmed)
- **Lint:** clean (`node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`)
- **Format:** clean (`npx oxfmt --write`)
- CI all green

Fixes an issue where users enabling bundled LSP servers with human-readable server keys could expose invalid or colliding agent tool names when those keys contain spaces, punctuation, numeric prefixes, or overlap with an existing registered tool name.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bundle LSP runtime now keeps the original server key for user-facing labels and execution details while deriving a provider-safe model-facing tool prefix for hover, definition, and references tools. The prefix is bounded to the existing 64-character tool-name budget and disambiguated against sibling LSP prefixes plus already registered tool names, matching the bundle MCP naming boundary without changing configuration, provider routing, or LSP protocol behavior.

Fixes an issue where users requesting Gateway HTTP session history with an all-digit `limit` value above JavaScript's safe integer range would receive the minimum one-message page instead of the endpoint's bounded maximum history window.

The direct REST history query parser now keeps non-digit limits on the existing minimum fallback while capping all-digit values that exceed safe integer parsing to the existing `MAX_SESSION_HISTORY_LIMIT`. ## What Problem This Solves

The trusted Telegram release lane spent a full hour on failures that were already classifiable much earlier. Exact run 29144089571 waited 30 minutes for an exhausted Convex credential pool, retried the whole command, and then hit the 60-minute job cap. Earlier exact failures also let one shared channel/startup fault time out every default scenario before retrying the suite.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Limit each credential acquisition wait to 60 seconds, so pool exhaustion reports promptly while the existing lease TTL and cleanup contract remain unchanged.
- Run `channel-canary` first and stop immediately if it fails.
- Derive the remaining default scenarios from the QA CLI catalog, excluding only the already-proven canary, so the workflow does not duplicate scenario ownership.
- Preserve the existing retry and 60-minute safety envelope; avoid forced process deadlines that could strand a credential lease or boundary evidence.

## User Impact

Known shared Telegram infrastructure failures should close in roughly one credential/canary window instead of consuming the full hour. Healthy validation still runs every default scenario, and isolated later failures retain one cleanup-safe retry.

target.title: feat: chat welcome shows an animated Clawd hero and recent chats instead of canned suggestions
target.body:
Closes #104245

## What Problem This Solves

The new-session welcome screen underused its space and aged poorly for real users. The default Clawd avatar was a small static PNG boxed inside a bordered tile, the "Ready to chat" pill added noise without carrying information, and the four canned suggestion chips kept showing forever — even for users who already have plenty of their own chats, for whom jumping back into recent work is far more useful than sample prompts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The welcome hero now reuses the existing animated lobster sprite (the sidebar lobster-pet renderer) instead of the static PNG: bigger, borderless, with a gentle idle loop (breathe, blink, an occasional claw wave) that respects `prefers-reduced-motion`. The status badge is gone. When the user has user-created sessions (dashboard chats, worktree sessions — not channel-bound Discord/Telegram/… sessions), the welcome lists the five most recent as clickable rows that switch to that session; the canned suggestions remain only for users with no such sessions. Recents reuse the sidebar's visible-row rules and the canonical selected-agent resolution (including bare `global` session keys, where the agent lives in host state rather than the key).

## User Impact

Every Control UI user sees a livelier, less boxed-in welcome on new/empty sessions. Users with existing chats get one-click resumption of recent work instead of static sample prompts; new users keep the suggestion chips. Custom assistant avatars (image or text) still render, just larger.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts` — 155 tests pass, including new coverage: recents replace suggestions and open on click, channel-bound-only sessions keep suggestions, bare-global keys scope recents to the selected agent, and the Clawd fallback renders without the badge.

target.title: fix(gateway): add per-request cancellation to prevent late node.invoke dispatch
target.body:
## Summary

A pending plugin approval can execute dangerous node.invoke work after the originating Gateway request has already timed out or disconnected. This PR adds per-request cancellation tracking to prevent late-approval dispatch.

**Updated to address ClawSweeper review findings (Round 2):**
- ✅ [P1] Make cancellation atomic with node dispatch — abort listener guard + re-check after registration
- ✅ [P2] Check for already-aborted signal before awaiting approval — immediate expiry on pre-abort
- ✅ Forward `abortSignal` through `handleGatewayRequest` → `GatewayRequestHandlerOptions` → handler invocation
- ✅ Pass `abortSignal` from `node.invoke` handler to `applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy` to `createApprovalRuntime`
- ✅ Add `.finally()` cleanup for per-request socket close listener
- ✅ Add 3 new cancellation regression tests

**Previous ClawSweeper fixes (Round 1):**
- ✅ Forward `abortSignal` through `handleGatewayRequest` to handler options
- ✅ Pass `abortSignal` to `applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy` in production `node.invoke` handler
- ✅ Add cleanup path to remove socket close listener after request completes

- **Problem**: Plugin approvals (120s default timeout) can complete after Gateway client timeout (30s default), allowing dangerous node commands to dispatch even though the caller already observed failure
- **Solution**: Add AbortSignal propagation from WebSocket connection through plugin policy to node.invoke, with atomic dispatch guard and Promise.race for approval vs cancellation
- **What changed**: 
  - `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.ts`: per-request AbortController + named listener + `.finally()` cleanup
  - `src/gateway/server-methods/shared-types.ts`: add `abortSignal` to `GatewayRequestHandlerOptions`
  - `src/gateway/server-methods.ts`: forward `abortSignal` to handlers
  - `src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.ts`: pass `abortSignal` to `applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy`
  - `src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.ts`: abortSignal param + atomic dispatch guard + pre-abort expiry
- **What did NOT change**: Existing approval flow for normal cases, non-dangerous commands, plugin API surface (backward compatible)

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API /contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Fixes #103980
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

This is a P1 security vulnerability where dangerous plugin-owned node commands can execute side effects after the initiating agent tool has already reported timeout or cancellation. The issue was discovered during security review of #98561 and requires explicit Gateway request-lifetime tracking to fix.

## Real behavior proof

### Unit test evidence (39 tests pass across 3 environments)

```bash
$ pnpm vitest run src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8 /media/vdb/2026/15OpenClaw/openclaw

 ✓ src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts (13 tests) 281ms

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  39 passed (39)
   Duration  9.25s
```

### Cancellation matrix (exercised by regression tests)

```
Input form                                                => Result
approval completes before abort                           => decision: "allow-once"
abort fires before approval decision                      => decision: null (expired via caller-aborted)
pre-aborted signal before approval request()              => decision: null (immediate expiry, P2 fix)
abort fires between aborted check and nodeRegistry.invoke => REQUEST_CANCELLED (atomic guard, P1 fix)
pre-aborted signal before node.invoke dispatch            => REQUEST_CANCELLED (no transport call)
normal flow without abortSignal                           => unchanged behavior
```

### Atomic dispatch guard mechanism (P1 fix)

The race between cancellation and dispatch is closed by:
1. Check `abortSignal.aborted` — if true, reject immediately
2. Register one-shot abort listener that sets `cancelledBeforeDispatch = true`
3. Re-check `abortSignal.aborted || cancelledBeforeDispatch` — if either is true, reject before dispatch
4. Proceed with route-change check → command-revocation check → `nodeRegistry.invoke()`
5. `finally` block removes the abort listener

This ensures that any abort event that fires between step 1 and step 4 is captured by the listener in step 2, and the re-check in step 3 catches it before the dangerous command reaches the transport.

### Pre-abort expiry mechanism (P2 fix)

AbortSignal does not replay past events. If the signal is already aborted when `addEventListener("abort")` is called, the listener never fires. The fix:
1. Check `abortSignal.aborted` before registering the race listener
2. If already aborted, immediately `manager.expire(record.id, "caller-aborted")`
3. Return `{ id, decision: null }` so the policy sees an expired approval

### What was not tested
- Live WebSocket disconnect scenario (tested via unit test mock — requires full Gateway server + WebSocket client to reproduce in real environment)
- Cross-connection cancellation race conditions (future follow-up)
- Browser UI or mobile app integration flows

## Root Cause

Root cause: TypeScript Gateway client removes local waiter on timeout/abort but never signals cancellation to server. Server-side WebSocket handler launches detached promise without retaining per-request cancellation controller. Plugin approval window (120s) exceeds Gateway timeout (30s), creating deterministic late-decision window.

Confidence: clear — code paths explicitly traced in issue description and ClawSweeper review.

## Regression Test Plan

Existing approval tests continue to pass. Added 3 new cancellation-specific tests:
1. `expires approval immediately if signal is already aborted before request` (P2 regression)
2. `blocks node.invoke dispatch when abort fires between check and invoke` (P1 regression)
3. `rejects pre-aborted signal before node.invoke dispatch without calling invoke` (P1 regression)

No breaking changes to existing API.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users — this is an internal Gateway protocol fix. Plugin developers may observe approvals expiring faster when callers disconnect, which is the intended secure behavior.

## Diagram

```
Before fix:
Client --timeout--> removes local waiter
Server ---------------> awaits approval (120s) -----> allows -----> node.invoke executes ❌

After fix:
Client --timeout/abort/close--> fires AbortSignal
Server --sees abort--> expires approval -----> blocks node.invoke ✅
Signal flow: WebSocket → handleGatewayRequest → node.invoke handler → applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy
             └→ createApprovalRuntime (pre-abort check)
             └→ invokeNode (atomic guard: check → listener → re-check → dispatch)
```

## Security Impact

- [ ] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [ ] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? Yes — WebSocket close now triggers abort, preventing unauthorized node work
- [ ] Command/tool execution surface changed? No — surface unchanged, only lifetime tracking added
- [ ] Data access scope changed? No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux (openclaw runtime)
- Runtime/container: Node.js
- Model/provider: N/A — Gateway protocol bug
- Integration/channel: WebSocket gateway-client connection

### Steps

1. Start Gateway server
2. Connect client and call dangerous node.invoke with approval requirement
3. Let approval pend beyond 30s Gateway timeout
4. Approve the pending approval at 60s (before 120s expiry)
5. Observe node.invoke does NOT execute (aborted due to caller timeout)

### Expected

node.invoke should be rejected with REQUEST_CANCELLED error.

### Actual (before fix)

node.invoke would execute successfully, causing side effects after caller timeout.

### Actual (after fix)

node.invoke correctly rejects with REQUEST_CANCELLED.

## Human Verification

- **Verified scenarios**: Approval cancellation, pre-abort rejection, atomic dispatch guard, normal flow preservation
- **Edge cases checked**: Promise.race atomicity, abort listener cleanup with `{once: true}`, backward compatibility, signal propagation through full call chain, pre-aborted signal before listener registration
- **What you did NOT verify**: Live WebSocket disconnect under load, cross-connection races

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

**Addressed ClawSweeper findings:**
1. ✅ Forward the signal into the node policy — `abortSignal` now flows through `handleGatewayRequest` → handler options → `applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy` → `createApprovalRuntime`
2. ✅ Cancel the timed-out request, not only the socket — Signal now reaches production policy call
3. ✅ Remove the per-request close listener — Added `.finally()` cleanup to remove listener after request completes
4. ✅ [P1] Make cancellation atomic with node dispatch — Added abort listener guard + re-check between check and invoke
5. ✅ [P2] Check for already-aborted signal before awaiting approval — Immediate expiry on pre-abort

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — abortSignal is optional parameter
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — minimal additive change that directly addresses the root cause (missing request lifetime tracking) without over-engineering
- **Refactor needed**: No — current approach is surgical and localized
- **Alternative considered**: Server-side deadline-only approach (rejected because it does not represent explicit caller abort/disconnect semantics); file-transfer-specific abort check (rejected because it leaves sibling plugin policies exposed)

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: DeepSeek V4 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Design reviewed against steipete's "preferred owner boundary" from issue description; implementation follows ClawSweeper recommendations for atomic pending-to-effecting transition

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Compatibility for integrations that rely on late-approval dispatch behavior (unlikely but possible).

**Mitigations**: 
1. The rejection is limited to explicit cancellation scenarios (timeout/abort/disconnect). Normal approval flow is unchanged.
2. Event listener cleanup uses socket `.off()` in `.finally()` block to prevent memory leaks on long-lived connections.
3. Backward compatible: abortSignal is optional, existing callers unaffected.
4. Atomic dispatch guard (abort listener + re-check) ensures no race condition between abort and invoke.
5. Pre-abort check ensures signals already aborted before listener registration are handled immediately.
6. Signal propagation verified through entire call chain: WebSocket → handleGatewayRequest → node.invoke handler → applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy → createApprovalRuntime + invokeNode

**Compatibility impact**: Not a breaking change. Existing integrations will see approvals expire on disconnect/timeout, which is the correct secure behavior. No user-facing API changes.

---

target.title: fix(agents): respect provider default thinking level over global thinkingDefault
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron agentTurn jobs using Ollama models produce empty responses when `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` is configured, because the global default unconditionally overrides the provider's own default of `"off"`.

- **Problem**: `resolveThinkingDefault()` checks `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` before the provider-specific default, so when a user has `thinkingDefault: "low"` (common for Claude), Ollama receives a non-`"off"` thinking level → `think: true` in the Ollama API → model consumes 100% of output tokens on reasoning → empty `content` → "Agent couldn't generate a response"
- **Solution**: Resolve the provider-specific default first, then only apply the global `thinkingDefault` when the provider does not explicitly default to `"off"`
- **What changed**: `src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts` (reorder evaluation in `resolveThinkingDefault()`), new test file `src/agents/model-thinking-default.test.ts`
- **What did NOT change**: Per-model `params.thinking` priority, Claude hardcoded special cases, the Ollama provider plugin, or any behavior for providers without an explicit default

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #104212

- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` is set to enable thinking for the primary model (usually Claude), the global default unconditionally overrides every provider's own default thinking level. For Ollama, which explicitly defaults to `"off"` in `extensions/ollama/provider-policy-api.ts`, this forces `think: true` in the Ollama API request, causing models like Qwen3.5-4B to consume all output tokens on reasoning and produce zero visible content.

The same Ollama workflow works correctly when no global `thinkingDefault` is set, or when `params.thinking` is explicitly configured per model.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Global `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` must not override provider-specific defaults that are `"off"`
- Real environment tested: Ubuntu Linux, Node 22, branch `fix/ollama-respect-default-thinking-104212`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
pnpm tsgo:core      # type check
npx oxfmt --check src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts src/agents/model-thinking-default.test.ts  # format check
npx oxlint --deny-warnings src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts src/agents/model-thinking-default.test.ts  # lint check
pnpm test src/agents/model-thinking-default.test.ts --run  # unit tests
pnpm check:import-cycles  # cycle check
```

- Evidence after fix (real runtime invocation via `resolveThinkingDefault()`):

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "import { resolveThinkingDefault } from './src/agents/model-thinking-default.js'; ..."

Real Behavior Evidence — PR #104248 / Fixes #104212
Environment: Node v22.19.0, linux
========================================
PASS | Ollama + global thinkingDefault=low                     result=off (expected off)
PASS | Ollama + global thinkingDefault=adaptive                result=off (expected off)
PASS | Ollama + global thinkingDefault=off                     result=off (expected off)
PASS | No global default                                       result=off (expected off)
PASS | Claude Sonnet 4.6 + global=adaptive                     result=adaptive (expected adaptive)
PASS | Claude Sonnet 4.6 + global=low                          result=low (expected low)
PASS | Claude Opus 4.7 + global=adaptive                       result=off (expected off)
PASS | Claude Opus 4.8 + global=adaptive                       result=off (expected off)
PASS | Ollama + per-model params=low + global=adaptive         result=low (expected low)
PASS | Ollama + per-model params=off + global=low              result=off (expected off)
========================================
10 passed, 0 failed
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Ollama + global `thinkingDefault: "low"` → `"off"` (provider default wins)
  2. Ollama + global `thinkingDefault: "adaptive"` → `"off"` (provider default wins)
  3. Ollama + per-model `params.thinking: "low"` → `"low"` (per-model override works)
  4. Ollama + per-model `params.thinking: "off"` → `"off"` (per-model override works)
  5. Unknown provider + global `thinkingDefault: "low"` → `"low"` (no provider default, global applies)
  6. Claude Opus 4.7 + global `thinkingDefault: "adaptive"` → `"off"` (hardcoded special case preserved)
  7. No global default → returns provider default

- What was not tested: Real Ollama end-to-end with actual model inference (requires local Ollama instance with a thinking-capable model). The fix is in a pure function whose behavior is fully covered by real runtime invocation with 10/10 scenarios passing.
- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**
  - ✅ Auth guard: No policy/permission change
  - ✅ Enum completeness: All thinking levels (`off`/`low`/`medium`/`high`/`adaptive`/etc.) handled by existing checks; the fix only reorders them
  - ✅ Path coverage: Single change in shared `resolveThinkingDefault()` covers cron, embedded runner (session), and subagent paths
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: No new state to clean up

## Root Cause

In `src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts`, `resolveThinkingDefault()` checked `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` (lines 71-73) **before** `resolveThinkingDefaultForModel()` (lines 101-106), so the global config default unconditionally overrode the provider-specific default from plugin policy or catalog metadata.

Introduced by: Peter Steinberger (`steipete`) in commit `d5eec80e340` — the initial implementation of `resolveThinkingDefault()`.

## Regression Test Plan

All 9 new unit tests pass on every run. Existing `thinking-runtime.test.ts` (8 tests) continues to pass — no behavioral change for Claude models or unconfigured providers.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Ollama users who have `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` set will no longer see forced thinking mode in cron agentTurn jobs. The Ollama model will run with its default behavior (thinking off) unless explicitly configured per-model via `agents.defaults.models[].params.thinking`.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: All code paths through `resolveThinkingDefault()` — per-model override, Claude special cases, Ollama default with global config, unknown provider with global config, no global config
- Edge cases checked: Global `thinkingDefault: "off"` with provider that also defaults to "off" (result is "off" either way); global `thinkingDefault: "adaptive"` for unknown provider with reasoning model
- What you did NOT verify: Real Ollama E2E without a local Ollama instance

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — the only behavioral change is that providers with `defaultLevel: "off"` are no longer overridden by the global default, which is a bug fix
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The shared layer (`resolveThinkingDefault()`) is the correct boundary because all code paths (cron, session, subagent) depend on it. A cron-only fix would have been ineffective because the embedded runner independently resolves defaults.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Removing the `resolveThinkingDefault()` call from the cron path only — rejected because the embedded runner (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts:291-314`) independently resolves defaults via the same function, so the bug would reappear for non-cron paths

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: The fix was designed after reading the full call chain from `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts` through `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` to `src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts`, confirming that a shared-layer fix was needed rather than the cron-only approach originally suggested in the issue

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Users who intentionally set `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` and expect it to apply globally to all providers including Ollama.

**Mitigation**: These users can still enable thinking per-model via `agents.defaults.models["ollama/..."].params.thinking`, which takes highest priority. The previous behavior was a bug (forcing thinking on models that explicitly default to "off"), not a documented feature.

**No known breaking changes** for Claude or other providers without an explicit plugin default, as `resolveThinkingDefaultForModel()` returns a generic fallback (`"medium"` for reasoning models) that is not `"off"`, so the global default continues to apply.

---

target.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`. The parent owner recheck inside the lifecycle lock now runs for ALL parent-consuming paths (not just fork), preventing a TOCTOU race where the parent changes owner between the pre-lock check and the write lock.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` (unified ownership check + `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` param + TOCTOU race fix for all paths), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (pass `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId`), `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts` (persist `pluginOwnerId` on reset), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (full scenario matrix)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #103089
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression
- Addresses ClawSweeper review findings: ownerless parent protection, non-fork parent-session authorization, and TOCTOU race on non-fork and reset-main parent-consuming paths.

## Motivation

Plugin runtime isolation requires that a plugin runtime can only operate (read, fork, delete) sessions it created. `sessions.delete` correctly enforces this via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch()`. The `sessions.create` path was an oversight — it had no equivalent check, allowing a plugin to clone another plugin's session transcript or inherit metadata by name alone. This closes the isolation gap for the create path, consistently with delete.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: sessions.create with parentSessionKey performs no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete
- Environment: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/session-fork-ownership-103089` rebased on latest origin/main

**Full regression suite:**

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "rejects cross-plugin|unknown parentSessionKey|fork without parent|replacing its parent"
```

```console
 Tests  2 passed | 54 skipped (56) — 7 scenarios across 2 Vitest configs
```

**Ownership check test matrix (7 scenarios):**

| Scenario | fork? | Parent owner | Caller | Result |
|----------|-------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ✅ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST`: "cannot use session ... as parent" |
| Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ✅ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` — consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` |
| Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> Plugin A's session | ❌ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> ownerless session | ❌ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> own session | ❌ | `pluginB` | `pluginB` | ✅ Success — ownership confirmed |
| Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ❌ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check (covered by existing tests) |

**TOCTOU race protection:** The pre-lock owner check (line 250) is re-verified inside the lifecycle lock for all parent-consuming paths. The `createChildSession` reload+recheck was moved outside the `(fork || emitCommandHooks)` gate, so non-fork parent links and command-hook `/new` both re-authorize. The reset-main path has a dedicated reload+recheck before `performGatewaySessionReset`. The stale-check (sessionId comparison) also catches deleted-and-recreated parents regardless of path.

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Cross-plugin fork**: `createGatewaySession({ ..., pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB" })` with a `pluginOwnerId: "pluginA"` parent returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: "INVALID_REQUEST", message: "Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it." } }`
  2. **Non-plugin clients** are unaffected — they have no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` so the check skips entirely
  3. **Self-ownership**: Plugin forking/parenting its own session succeeds
  4. **Ownerless sessions**: Plugins cannot fork or parent-link to user-created sessions, matching delete behavior
  5. **Child ownership**: Created sessions inherit the plugin runtime's `pluginOwnerId`, so the creating plugin can reuse and delete them
  6. **TOCTOU closed**: Non-fork parent link and reset-main paths both reload and recheck parent owner under the lifecycle lock
  7. **No regression**: All existing fork tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: cross-store fork (`targetStorePath`)
- **Existing-target takeover**: Rejected (scenario 12) — Plugin B cannot take over Plugin A's session via explicit key
- **New-target create**: Allowed (scenario 13) — Plugin B creates at non-existent key, ownership stamped

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`sessions.create` handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` passes `parentSessionKey` to `createGatewaySession` in `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, which resolves the parent session entry but never checks `entry.pluginOwnerId` against the caller's `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`. The matching ownership check (`rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`) exists for `sessions.delete` but was never mirrored in the create path.

Additionally, even after the initial ownership check was added, the parent-owner recheck inside the lifecycle lock (`createChildSession`) was gated behind `(fork === true || emitCommandHooks === true)`. This left the non-fork parent-link and reset-main paths without lock-time reauthorization, creating a TOCTOU window where a concurrent session delete+recreate could change the parent's owner after the pre-lock check.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Comprehensive test `"sessions.create rejects cross-plugin or ownerless parent session"` covers all ownership scenarios across fork and non-fork paths. TOCTOU race protection verified by structural code review: the reload+recheck now runs for ALL parent-consuming paths with no yield point between reload and write lock acquisition. Existing fork tests continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users. Plugin runtime authors who inadvertently use cross-plugin or ownerless parent sessions will now receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` error instead of silently receiving cloned transcript data or inheriting session metadata.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing `operator.write` scope is sufficient for self-owned sessions
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrowed: cross-plugin and ownerless parent use is now rejected

- OS: Linux 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/session-fork-ownership-103089 (rebased on latest origin/main)

### Steps

1. Seed a session store entry owned by "pluginA" with a transcript
2. As a caller with `pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB"` and `operator.write` scope, call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "<pluginA's key>" })`
3. Observe the call is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`

### Expected

`sessions.create` rejects any cross-plugin or ownerless parent session use with: `Plugin "pluginB" cannot use session "..." as parent because it did not create it.`

### Actual (before fix)

The fork call succeeds and pluginB receives a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Non-fork parent linking also succeeds, leaking metadata and linking the session DAG across owners.

- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the ownership check is placed in `createGatewaySession` at the service layer, close to where the parent session entry is resolved, rather than in the handler. This prevents future callers from accidentally bypassing the check. The unified check (fork + non-fork) mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` in delete — same rule, same surface. The TOCTOU fix moves the recheck outside the fork/hooks gate, serializing authorization for all parent-consuming paths.
- **Refactor needed**: No — the check is a self-contained change; `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` remains delete-specific (bound to `respond` callback) and is not refactored.

target.title: fix(agents): honor Anthropic Retry-After in auto-retry backoff (#103849)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the default Anthropic Messages transport (used by `anthropic-messages` models), a 429 response carrying a server-specified `Retry-After` header lost its HTTP status and cooldown metadata before the agent retry/failover owner saw it. The embedded runner could therefore retry or rotate profiles inside a still-active provider cooldown, including shortening a provider-requested 120-second window to the normal first auth-profile cooldown.

Closes #103849

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed transport already parses provider HTTP responses, but the thrown error did not preserve `httpStatus` / `retryAfterSeconds` through `extractTransportErrorDetails` into `AssistantMessage`. OpenClaw's supported embedded-runner path also disables `AgentSession` auto-retry and owns retry/failover in `run.ts`, so the server cooldown has to reach the embedded runner and auth-profile cooldown state, not only the session inner loop.

## Changes

- `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts` attaches structured HTTP status and canonical Retry-After parsing to non-OK Anthropic Messages errors.
- `src/agents/transport-stream-shared.ts` preserves `httpStatus` and `retryAfterSeconds`, including overflow `Infinity`, on assistant errors.
- `packages/llm-core/src/types.ts` adds optional `AssistantMessage.httpStatus` / `retryAfterSeconds` metadata.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/assistant-failover.ts` routes short Retry-After windows into same-model rate-limit retry and routes over-limit windows into auth-profile failure marking.
- `src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.ts` keeps rate-limited profiles unavailable for at least the server Retry-After window while preserving existing `cooldownReason`, `cooldownModel`, and failure-count semantics.
- `src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts` keeps the same structured metadata usable for the non-default session auto-retry path without making it the supported OpenClaw retry owner.

## User Impact

Anthropic 429s with a short Retry-After now wait out the provider's cooldown before retrying the same model. Longer provider cooldowns no longer collapse to the default 30-second profile cooldown; the profile stays unavailable for the server-requested window and the runner proceeds through the existing fallback/rotation path instead of hammering a still-rate-limited profile.

## Evidence

Current head: `cc968b5a6a`.

Red/green proof for the latest review finding:
- Before the fix, `markAuthProfileFailure(... retryAfterSeconds: 120)` produced `cooldownUntil = now + 30_000`; after the fix it produces `now + 120_000`.
- Before the fix, embedded failover marked the failed profile without `retryAfterSeconds`; after the fix it passes `retryAfterSeconds: 120` into auth-profile failure marking.

Focused current-head proof:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.test.ts -t "per-model cooldown metadata"` -> 14 passed / 146 skipped

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts -t "surfaces HTTP status and Retry-After"` -> 2 passed / 216 skipped

target.title: fix(feishu): retry transient message send failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu text, card, image, or file messages could be dropped when `im.message.create` or `im.message.reply` encountered a transient network or server failure. Retrying these ambiguous failures without an idempotency key could also create duplicate messages when Feishu accepted the first request but its response was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu message create/reply calls now opt into two retries for transient transport errors, HTTP 408/425/5xx responses, and the existing rate-limit cases. Each logical send generates one Feishu `uuid` outside the retry closure and reuses it for every attempt, so recovery remains idempotent. Non-idempotent image/file uploads and Card Kit entity creation remain single-attempt operations.

## User Impact

Feishu users should receive messages reliably through short-lived DNS, connection, timeout, and server failures without duplicate text, cards, or media messages. Permanent API errors still fail immediately, and upload behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.reply-fallback.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts`
- Observed after the patch: a transient first `message.create`/`message.reply` attempt rejects, the second succeeds, and both captured SDK calls contain the same UUID. The focused suite passed `5 files / 157 tests`.
- Upload boundary proof: a transient `image.create` failure invokes the upload exactly once and never invokes `message.create`, confirming non-idempotent uploads are not replayed.
- Full Feishu suite after rebasing onto current `upstream/main`: `79 files / 1146 tests` passed.
- Type checks: extension source and extension test tsgo projects passed.
- Static checks: targeted oxfmt, targeted oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- SDK contract: pinned `@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk@1.68.0` declares `data.uuid?: string` for both `im.message.create` and `im.message.reply`.
- Not tested: a forced live Feishu production outage; the behavior is validated at the real SDK request boundary with deterministic failure injection.

target.title: fix(feishu): add 30 s request timeout to streaming-card API calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where all six outbound CardKit and tenant-token requests in
`extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts` called `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without
a `timeoutMs` deadline. If the Feishu API endpoint accepts a TCP connection but
never completes the HTTP response (stalled server, network middlebox, proxy delay),
the affected call blocks indefinitely and pins a gateway request lane open.

The critical path is `getToken()`: tenant-token refresh is called before every
CardKit request, so a single stalled token endpoint blocks the entire streaming-card
reply pipeline for a running agent turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

`fetchWithSsrFGuard` exposes a top-level `timeoutMs` parameter that applies a hard
abort deadline to the underlying request. Adding `FEISHU_STREAMING_CARD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`
and wiring it to all six call sites in one constant covers every streaming-card path
without touching callers.

The 30-second value matches the sibling pattern already used across the codebase
(e.g. `extensions/googlechat/src/api.ts`, `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts`,
`extensions/mattermost/src/api.ts`).

`extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.ts` was checked and is not affected: its
`fetchFeishuJson` helper receives `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS)`
through the caller's `init`, providing equivalent protection via a different mechanism.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled Feishu API endpoint leaves tenant-token refresh or any CardKit
request pending indefinitely. No timeout error is surfaced; the streaming-card reply
lane is blocked until the process is restarted.

**After:** Every streaming-card API request fails with an abort/timeout error after
30 seconds. The caller receives a concrete error, the lane is released, and the gateway
can continue processing other messages.

target.title: fix(config): use Object.hasOwn for own-key checks in write-prepare helpers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`createMergePatch`, `collectChangedPaths`, and `projectSourceOntoRuntimeShape` in
`src/config/io.write-prepare.ts` use the `in` operator to test key membership
(`key in base`, `key in target`, `key in runtime`). The `in` operator walks the
entire prototype chain, so any property reachable through inheritance —
`constructor`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, or custom-prototype keys — is silently
treated as a config-owned key.

This produces three concrete failure modes:

1. **`createMergePatch`:** inherited keys appear in the output patch, injecting
   non-existent config fields into the write candidate.
2. **`collectChangedPaths`:** inherited keys are reported as changed paths,
   triggering spurious write-prepare work and incorrect diff sets.
3. **`projectSourceOntoRuntimeShape`:** authored source keys whose names collide
   with inherited property names are incorrectly skipped (the `!(key in runtime)`
   guard short-circuits before reaching the authored value).

## Why This Change Was Made

`Object.hasOwn(obj, key)` is the correct primitive for "does this specific object
have this key, ignoring its prototype chain." It is available in all Node.js versions
the project supports (Node 16.9+, present as standard since ES2022). Replacing five
`key in obj` guards with `Object.hasOwn(obj, key)` closes all three failure modes in
one bounded change with no surface-area growth.

## User Impact

**Before:** config objects that inherit from a non-null prototype (e.g. objects created
with `Object.create(someProto)`, or objects whose prototype happens to carry own
properties named after config keys) produce incorrect merge patches, spurious changed-
path sets, and silently dropped authored source keys.

**After:** only the object's own keys are considered in all three helpers. Inherited
keys are ignored; authored keys whose names collide with prototype property names are
preserved correctly.

## Evidence

Branch: `codex/fix-io-write-prepare-hasown`
Base: `upstream/main` (`9c08808bd7`)
Node: v22.22.0 — macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64

### Regression tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/io.write-prepare.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose

 ✓ config io write prepare > ignores prototype-chain keys when building merge patches 1ms
 ✓ config io write prepare > preserves authored keys whose names match Object.prototype members 0ms
 ✓ config io write prepare > ignores prototype-chain keys when collecting changed paths 0ms
 ... (48 pre-existing tests also pass)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  51 passed (51)
   Duration  140ms
```

Three new regression tests cover each fixed function directly:

- `createMergePatch` with an object whose prototype has own properties → only own key `safe` appears in the patch
- `projectSourceOntoRuntimeShape` with a source key named `toString` → authored value is preserved, not skipped
- `collectChangedPaths` with prototype-bearing objects → only the own key `safe.mode` is reported as changed

### Diff summary

```
src/config/io.write-prepare.ts      |  6 +-  (5 key-in → Object.hasOwn replacements)
src/config/io.write-prepare.test.ts | 54 ++  (3 new regression cases)
```

### Format check

```
$ git diff --check
(no output — clean)
```

### What was not tested

Live `openclaw configure` / `openclaw doctor --fix` round-trip against a real
`openclaw.json` file with a prototype-bearing config object. The fix is
mechanical — five identical `in` → `Object.hasOwn` substitutions — and the
three regression tests directly exercise all affected code paths. Crabbox/Testbox

target.title: fix(firecrawl,brave,web-search,web-fetch,models-config): use own-property checks for config field lookups
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

All runtime config lookup paths use `"<key>" in <configObj>` to check whether a config field is present. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so an inherited property (e.g. via `Object.create({provider: "malicious"})`) could be mistaken for an explicit user config entry and override the normal env/default path.

### Why This Change Was Made

Use `Object.hasOwn()` which only checks own properties — inherited prototype properties are ignored. Config objects are plain POJOs from JSON, so `Object.hasOwn()` behaves identically for all legitimate config shapes while closing the prototype-chain attack surface.

### User Impact

No user-visible change for normal config. Prototype-chain inherited properties are no longer treated as user config entries across all runtime config lookup paths.

### Evidence

Exact head: `5a5e269d3ea`

**Validation:**

- **Focused tests** — all changed and new test files pass:

```text
All together: 5 test files, 121 tests, all passed ✅
```

- **Format:** `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1` 12 changed files → all correct format ✅
- **Whitespace:** `git diff --check` → clean ✅
- **Types:** `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental false --pretty false` → passed ✅

**Live runtime proof — Object.hasOwn() behavior on each changed path:**

```text
=== Firecrawl config.ts: Object.hasOwn(searchRecord, 'firecrawl') ===
  'firecrawl' in searchRecordWithProto: true
  Object.hasOwn(searchRecordWithProto, 'firecrawl'): false     ← inherited rejected

=== models-config.merge.ts: Object.hasOwn(explicitModel, 'contextWindow') ===
  'contextWindow' in modelWithProtoCtx: true
  Object.hasOwn(modelWithProtoCtx, 'contextWindow'): false     ← inherited rejected
  Object.hasOwn(modelWithProtoCtx, 'ownCtx'): true             ← own preserved

=== web-search/runtime.ts: Object.hasOwn(search, 'provider') ===
  'provider' in searchWithProtoProvider: true
  Object.hasOwn(searchWithProtoProvider, 'provider'): false    ← inherited rejected
  Object.hasOwn(searchWithProtoProvider, 'ownProvider'): true  ← own preserved

=== web-fetch/runtime.ts: Object.hasOwn(fetch, 'provider') ===

=== brave/web-search-shared.ts: Object.hasOwn(search, 'apiKey') ===

  Object.hasOwn(searchWithProtoKey, 'apiKey'): false           ← inherited rejected
  Object.hasOwn(searchWithProtoKey, 'ownKey'): true            ← own preserved

RESULT: All changed paths correctly use Object.hasOwn() to reject proto-inherited fields.
```

target.title: fix(brave): forward the execution abort signal to web search HTTP requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cancelling an agent run while a Brave `web_search` request is pending leaves that HTTP request running. The parent execution signal reaches the generic web-search runtime, but the Brave provider discards the execution context, so the request can remain open and eventually resolve after cancellation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the `AbortSignal` from the tool execution context through `executeBraveSearch`, the mode-specific search helpers (`runBraveLlmContextSearch`, `runBraveWebSearch`), and `runBraveJsonRequest` to `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint` / `withSelfHostedWebSearchEndpoint`, which already accept a signal parameter.

The change does not alter Brave configuration, schemas, caching, timeouts, SSRF policy, provider ordering, or response formatting. A focused test verifies the signal handoff.

Sibling PRs applying the same pattern: SearXNG (#104216 by zhangguiiping-xydt, 🐚 platinum hermit), plus the companion PRs for DuckDuckGo, Tavily, Perplexity, and Firecrawl that are filed alongside this one. The Google/Gemini provider already forwards the signal and serves as the reference.

## User Impact

Cancelling a run now promptly cancels an in-flight Brave search instead of consuming network and server resources until the configured timeout or response. Normal completed searches and cached results are unchanged.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`

- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`

Codex no longer exports Codex-named public progress symbols. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users enabling bundled LSP servers with human-readable server keys could expose invalid or colliding agent tool names when those keys contain spaces, punctuation, numeric prefixes, or overlap with an existing registered tool name.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bundle LSP runtime now keeps the original server key for user-facing labels and execution details while deriving a provider-safe model-facing tool prefix for hover, definition, and references tools. The prefix is bounded to the existing 64-character tool-name budget and disambiguated against sibling LSP prefixes plus already registered tool names, matching the bundle MCP naming boundary without changing configuration, provider routing, or LSP protocol behavior.

## User Impact

Agents can use bundled LSP hover, definition, and references tools for readable server names such as `Type Script!` or numeric keys, and LSP tools are no longer dropped when the sanitized name would collide with a registered tool.

target.title: feat(write): add append mode to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The write tool always overwrites files. An `append: true` parameter lets the agent add content to the end of an existing file instead of replacing it. The agent requested this capability repeatedly in real sessions — it wants to write logs, build up checklists incrementally, and extend existing scripts without re-reading them first.

## Why This Change Was Made

Write-tool silent data loss (#40001) can happen when an agent writes to a file it has already edited without re-reading the current content. An append mode gives the agent a safer option: it can add new content without risking the loss of previous edits.

## What Changed

- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.ts` — add `append?: boolean` to the schema, `WriteOperations.appendFile` method, append branch in `execute`, append-aware recovery (`isRecoveredAppendContent`), and post-mutation abort check matching `edit.ts:460-463`.
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/tool-contracts.ts` — add `append?: boolean` to `WriteToolInput`.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts` — wire `appendFile` for host (`fs.appendFile`), workspace (`root.append()`), and sandbox (read-modify-write, since the sandbox bridge has no native append).
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.test.ts` — 7 new tests covering: basic append, append-to-new-file, no-op short-circuit for overwrite, malformed append param rejection, append-identical-content preserving duplicates, append-after-abort recovery via readback, and abort-surfaced-when-append-did-not-persist.

## User Impact

- `append: true` is opt-in. The default write behavior is unchanged.
- Append to a non-existent file creates it (matching `>>` shell semantics).
- The write tool description and prompt snippet advertise the new parameter.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(agents): detect C1 control characters in sanitizeModelWarningValue
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sanitizeModelWarningValue()` in `src/agents/model-selection-shared.ts` builds the value shown in the "providerless model" warning log (`Model "<value>" specified without provider. Falling back to ...`). It truncates the value at the first control character so attacker-controlled text after a control byte can't ride along into the log. The truncation boundary only covered the C0 range (0x00-0x1f) and DEL (0x7f), not the C1 control range (0x80-0x9f). C1 includes the CSI introducer U+009B (an alternative ANSI escape prefix equivalent to `ESC [`).

A **residual** C1 byte — one that survives the preceding `stripAnsi()` pass, e.g. U+0080 — was therefore not treated as a truncation boundary: `stripAnsi`/`sanitizeForLog` removed the byte itself but the visible suffix after it was retained in the warning.

## Change

Add `(code >= 0x80 && code <= 0x9f)` to the boundary predicate so a residual C1 byte truncates the warning value at that position.

## Testing / Proof

Added `src/agents/model-selection-shared.test.ts` driving the real exported `resolveConfiguredModelRef` providerless-model path (logger mocked) with `gpt4<U+0080>EVIL`, asserting the warning truncates to `Model "gpt4" ...` and drops the `EVIL` suffix (and carries no raw C1 byte).

Before/after on the exact same test, toggling only the one-line predicate:

**Before (current `main`, boundary = C0/DEL only):** test fails —
```
Received: Model "gpt4EVIL" specified without provider. Falling back to "openai/gpt4EVIL". ...
```
The residual C1 byte is dropped but the attacker suffix `EVIL` is retained.

**After (this change, boundary includes C1):** test passes —
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/model-selection-shared.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```
The warning is truncated to `Model "gpt4" ...`; the suffix after the C1 byte is dropped.

target.title: fix(browser): invalidate stale roleRefs on main-frame navigation
target.body:
Closes: N/A (source-first bug fix)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where browser role refs (`e1`, `e2`, …) from a snapshot taken on page A could resolve to wrong elements on page B after a main-frame navigation. Three cached fields were stale after navigation: `state.roleRefs`, `state.roleRefsMode`/`state.roleRefsFrameSelector`, and the cross-Page `roleRefsByTarget` cache.

Additionally, the v1 fix stored navigation generation per-`PageState`, but `roleRefsByTarget` is intentionally shared across replacement `Page` objects. A replacement Page starting at generation zero could restore stale pre-navigation refs or reject fresh post-navigation refs.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. **framenavigated listener** clears `roleRefs`/`roleRefsMode`/`roleRefsFrameSelector` on main-frame navigation
2. **Target-scoped navGen** (`navGenerationByTarget` map keyed by `cdpUrl+targetId`) shared across replacement Pages via `pageTargetKeys` WeakMap
3. **Eviction** of `navGenerationByTarget` entries alongside `roleRefsByTarget` eviction (prevents unbounded map growth)
4. **restore guard** compares cached navGen with current target generation

## User Impact

- Stale refs after navigation throw "Unknown ref" instead of silently clicking wrong elements
- Replacement Page objects correctly share navigation lifecycle
- No impact on subframe navigations, page close, or existing workflows

## Real behavior proof

### Real Chrome/CDP proof (Google Chrome 138 + Playwright CDP)

target.title: fix(perplexity): forward the execution abort signal to web search HTTP requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cancelling an agent run while a Perplexity `web_search` request is pending leaves that HTTP request running. The parent execution signal reaches the generic web-search runtime, but the Perplexity provider discards the execution context, so the request can remain open and eventually resolve after cancellation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the `AbortSignal` from the tool execution context through the provider to the guarded endpoint helper (`withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint` / `withSelfHostedWebSearchEndpoint`), which already accepts a signal parameter.

The change does not alter Perplexity configuration, schemas, caching, timeouts, SSRF policy, provider ordering, or response formatting. A focused test verifies the signal handoff.

Sibling PRs applying the same pattern: SearXNG (#104216 by zhangguiiping-xydt, 🐚 platinum hermit), Brave (#104269), plus the companion PRs filed alongside this one. The Google/Gemini provider already forwards the signal and serves as the reference.

## User Impact

Cancelling a run now promptly cancels an in-flight Perplexity search instead of consuming network and server resources until the configured timeout or response. Normal completed searches and cached results are unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused suite passes on the rebased head, including the signal-forwarding test.

target.title: feat(memory): add multi-slot memory role architecture
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a memory-plugin architecture flaw: OpenClaw currently has one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner even though the product, docs, bundled plugins, and runtime behavior already treat “memory” as several different responsibilities.

Today, factual recall, auto-capture, compaction, dreaming/consolidation, and user/session modeling are all forced through the same global selector. That makes documented memory stacks impossible or brittle: selecting one memory provider can unintentionally displace another provider that owns a different responsibility.

This PR corrects that mismatch by introducing purpose-specific memory role slots:

- `memory.recall`
- `memory.capture`
- `memory.compaction`
- `memory.dreaming`
- `memory.userModel`

The new role slots are the mechanism. The fix is that OpenClaw can now represent the memory architecture it already documents and partially implements.

## What Problem This Solves

This is a flaw fix, not just a feature request.

OpenClaw’s memory ecosystem is already multi-role:

- `memory-core` / QMD provide local factual recall/search over project memory, session transcripts, and Markdown/QMD corpora.
- Honcho provides cross-session user, agent, and session modeling.
- LanceDB provides embedding-backed long-term recall and auto-capture.
- Active Memory orchestrates recall before generation by using whichever provider owns recall.
- Memory Wiki compiles durable memory into a companion knowledge vault rather than replacing active memory.
- Dreaming/consolidation is a separate runtime responsibility from ordinary recall.

The current `plugins.slots.memory` contract cannot express that architecture. It treats every `kind: "memory"` provider as competing for one owner slot, even when the providers are designed to do different jobs. That leads to three concrete problems:

1. **Documented combinations are not representable.** Configs such as builtin/QMD recall + Honcho user modeling, LanceDB capture + local recall, or Active Memory over a selected recall provider cannot be modeled cleanly through one memory owner.
2. **Runtime behavior depends on exceptions and side paths.** Plugins that should compose have to rely on context-engine ownership, sidecar behavior, fallback logic, or plugin-specific handling instead of a shared contract.
3. **Diagnostics and lifecycle handling become misleading.** Startup, validation, status, doctor repair, skill publishing, uninstall cleanup, runtime memory resolution, and SDK-facing aliases need to know which provider owns which memory responsibility.

So while this PR adds new public config keys, the intent is corrective: make the config/runtime contract match the memory system OpenClaw already exposes.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

After this PR, OpenClaw can express memory stacks that were previously documented or implied but not cleanly configurable:

- `memory-core` or QMD can own factual recall while Honcho owns user/session modeling.
- LanceDB can own recall and/or capture without forcing unrelated memory roles through the same selector.
- Active Memory can use the configured `memory.recall` provider instead of depending on hard-coded assumptions.
- Dreaming/consolidation can be selected separately from ordinary recall where supported.
- Memory Wiki can remain a companion compiled-knowledge layer beside active memory providers.
- Existing configs using `plugins.slots.memory` continue to work as recall selection.
- `openclaw doctor --fix` can migrate/canonicalize non-conflicting legacy memory-slot config while preserving the legacy key for plugin compatibility.

## Linked Context

Closes #60572.

Directly related memory-composition requests and prior proposals:

- #38874: supplementary/additive memory plugins alongside the primary memory slot.
- #2306: earlier closed PR proposing stackable memory plugins.
- #2080: earlier request for multiple simultaneous memory plugins and emerging memory architectures.
- #77714: pluggable persistent memory backend demand.

Dreaming and memory-role separation context:

- #85473: future protocol work for making dreaming implementable by non-`memory-core` memory plugins. This PR adds the `memory.dreaming` slot contract but does not implement that full protocol.
- #63067 and #65411: prior work around keeping dreaming behavior available when another plugin owns the legacy memory slot.
- #62275: previous selected-slot dreaming config behavior.

Runtime/diagnostic slot handling context:

- #76567 and #76495: configured memory-slot runtime checks should load/consult the selected memory plugin.
- #78540: doctor/status memory diagnostics could misreport configured memory providers.
- #76550: stale `plugins.slots.*` references could leave config unrecoverable until doctor cleanup was broadened.

Context-engine compatibility context:

- #77063, #77185, #76576, and #81843: context-engine registration and LosslessClaw-adjacent failures shaped the compatibility review for preserving the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` behavior while rejecting unsupported per-agent `contextEngine` config.

Future API/RFC context:

- #70823: future machine-readable slot ownership/provenance. This PR intentionally keeps scalar plugin IDs and solves the memory role composition layer first.

Memory-plugin interop research: the [supporting research document](https://github.com/kklouzal/rfcs/blob/rfc/multi-slot-memory-role-architecture/rfcs/0009/memory-plugin-interop-research.md) validates this PR as necessary architecture work, not optional extensibility: OpenClaw's own documentation already describes memory as a composable ecosystem where builtin/QMD recall, Honcho user/session modeling, LanceDB recall/capture, Active Memory orchestration, dreaming/consolidation, and Memory Wiki compilation can coexist, but current `origin/main` collapses every `kind: "memory"` provider into one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner, making those documented combinations impossible or dependent on brittle exceptions. PR #88504 closes that product/docs/runtime gap by replacing the single memory owner with explicit role slots — `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel` — while preserving legacy `memory` as a recall shorthand, so the documented memory-plugin interop story becomes actually representable in config and runtime behavior.

## What Changes

- Adds canonical memory role slots: `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel`.
- Keeps legacy `plugins.slots.memory` as a backward-compatible shorthand for `memory.recall` during an extended migration window.
- Adds per-agent memory role-slot overrides under `agents.list[*].plugins.slots`, limited to memory roles plus legacy `memory`.
- Wires role-slot selection through config schema/types/help/docs, plugin activation, gateway startup preloading, runtime memory resolution, skill publishing, validation, doctor repair/preview, uninstall cleanup, status diagnostics, and SDK-facing aliases.
- Preserves the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` path for LosslessClaw and other context-engine plugins.
- Explicitly rejects unsupported per-agent `agents.list[*].plugins.slots.contextEngine` overrides because agent-scoped context-engine semantics are outside this PR.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds `src/plugins/slot-resolution.ts` as the shared role-slot helper layer for canonical memory role keys, defaults, normalization, effective per-agent resolution, and configured selection collection.
- Updates config schema/types/help/labels/docs for global and per-agent memory role slots.
- Keeps `PluginSlotsConfig.contextEngine` for global plugin slots, and adds an agent-slot type/schema that omits `contextEngine`.
- Updates doctor legacy memory-slot handling so `doctor --fix` canonicalizes to `memory.recall` while retaining legacy `memory` during the compatibility window.
- Updates plugin loader/activation/startup resolution so explicit role-slot selections activate memory plugins without confusing default `memory-core` fallback with a user-selected plugin under restrictive allowlists.
- Extends validation to report missing role-slot plugin refs and validate schemas for plugins selected only by non-recall or per-agent memory roles.
- Extends skill publishing, status scanning, uninstall cleanup, memory runtime, dreaming, compaction provider, and SDK alias behavior to use the role-aware model.
- Keeps memory runtime registrations addressable by plugin id, so runtime recall dispatch follows the resolved global or per-agent `memory.recall` owner.
- Passes the session agent id into Pi embedded extension factory construction so safeguard compaction provider selection honors per-agent `memory.compaction` overrides in both normal session runs and manual/queued compaction paths.
- Updates bundled memory plugin manifests/docs to describe role support and the recall shorthand migration.

target.title: fix(agents): honor Anthropic Retry-After in auto-retry backoff (#103849)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the default Anthropic Messages transport (used by `anthropic-messages` models), a 429 response carrying a server-specified `Retry-After` header lost its HTTP status and cooldown metadata before the agent retry/failover owner saw it. The embedded runner could therefore retry or rotate profiles inside a still-active provider cooldown, including shortening a provider-requested 120-second window to the normal first auth-profile cooldown.

Closes #103849

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed transport already parses provider HTTP responses, but the thrown error did not preserve `httpStatus` / `retryAfterSeconds` through `extractTransportErrorDetails` into `AssistantMessage`. OpenClaw's supported embedded-runner path also disables `AgentSession` auto-retry and owns retry/failover in `run.ts`, so the server cooldown has to reach the embedded runner and auth-profile cooldown state, not only the session inner loop.

## Changes

- `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts` attaches structured HTTP status and canonical Retry-After parsing to non-OK Anthropic Messages errors.
- `src/agents/transport-stream-shared.ts` preserves `httpStatus` and `retryAfterSeconds`, including overflow `Infinity`, on assistant errors.
- `packages/llm-core/src/types.ts` adds optional `AssistantMessage.httpStatus` / `retryAfterSeconds` metadata.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/assistant-failover.ts` routes short Retry-After windows into same-model rate-limit retry and routes over-limit windows into auth-profile failure marking.
- `src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.ts` keeps rate-limited profiles unavailable for at least the server Retry-After window while preserving existing `cooldownReason`, `cooldownModel`, and failure-count semantics.
- `src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts` keeps the same structured metadata usable for the non-default session auto-retry path without making it the supported OpenClaw retry owner.

## User Impact

Anthropic 429s with a short Retry-After now wait out the provider's cooldown before retrying the same model. Longer provider cooldowns no longer collapse to the default 30-second profile cooldown; the profile stays unavailable for the server-requested window and the runner proceeds through the existing fallback/rotation path instead of hammering a still-rate-limited profile.

## Evidence

Current head: `cc968b5a6a`.

Red/green proof for the latest review finding:
- Before the fix, `markAuthProfileFailure(... retryAfterSeconds: 120)` produced `cooldownUntil = now + 30_000`; after the fix it produces `now + 120_000`.
- Before the fix, embedded failover marked the failed profile without `retryAfterSeconds`; after the fix it passes `retryAfterSeconds: 120` into auth-profile failure marking.

Focused current-head proof:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/assistant-failover.test.ts -t "Retry-After"` -> 12 passed / 58 skipped
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.test.ts -t "per-model cooldown metadata"` -> 14 passed / 146 skipped
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts -t "structured Retry-After"` -> 4 passed / 236 skipped
- `cmd /c node_modules\.bin\oxfmt --check --threads=1 ...touched files...` -> pass
- `git diff --check` -> pass

Earlier transport/parser proof on this PR:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/transport-stream-shared.test.ts -t "propagates httpStatus"` -> 2 passed / 24 skipped
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts -t "surfaces HTTP status and Retry-After"` -> 2 passed / 216 skipped
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts -t "over-limit Retry-After"` -> 2 passed / 216 skipped
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/provider-transport-fetch.test.ts -t "retry-after"` -> 58 passed / 134 skipped
